full_judgment:
7. Mr Syed Humayun Kabir Khadem, learned Advocate appearing in support of the Rule, after placing the petition and the two judgments of the courts below, contended that the appellate Court did not at all advert to the findings and decisions arrived at by the trial Court and the impugned judgment having not been a proper judgment of reversal, the same cannot be sustained in law. It was further contended by the learned Advocate that pre-emptor failed to prove his alleged date of knowledge of the kabala under the pre-emption proceeding through legal evidence and the petitioner could prove by legal evidence that the pre-emptor had clear and definite knowledge of the transfer matter since the purchase of the case land by the pre-emptee. 

 15. From the pleading, evidences and materials on record, it appears to me that the pre-emptor failed to prove his alleged date of knowledge through uncontroverted legal evidence. The trial Court on a proper discussion and consideration of evidences of both the parties came to the finding that the pre-emptor failed to prove the alleged date of knowledge and the case is hopelessly barred by limitation. The court of appeal without proper discussion of the evidences of the parties specially of the evidences from the side of the pre-emptee and without adverting to the material findings and decisions on which the trial Court''s judgment rested, reversed the decision arrived at by the trial Court on the question of limitation. The lower appellate Court being the last and final court of fact was required to discuss the evidences of the parties more so when it was going to reverse the decision of the trial Court. I have given my anxious consideration to the pleadings, evidences and materials on record and I am of this view that the judgment of the lower appellate Court is a slipshod judgment and the same was not a proper judgment of reversal and the lower appellate Court committed a substantial error of law in reversing the decision of the trial Court on the question of limitation. 

 19. In view of my discussions and observations made above, I hold that lower appellate Court totally misdirected itself in its approach on the question of limitation and the impugned judgment of reversal suffers from clear impropriety and also legal infirmity and the same cannot be sustained in law.
